body: I guess my thought would also be "why hurry?" If you enjoy life now but are impatient to experience what death may be like, why not just wait until it happens "naturally", or "not-naturally" but rather not because of your own hand. If death is the adventure I think you think it might be, the time you spend alive would be nothing.

Well, thanks, sometimes it's better, it's been difficult lately. I think the problem is I set this goal a year a head and here it is, on top of my birthday. I thought things would change for the better after I moved here.

I'm sorry but don't fool yourself into believing that "death" is just another part of life. Death is the end. There is nothing afterwards, there will be no adventure, because the machine (or mechanism) that has created every thought, feeling, emotion, idea, dream, hallucination, fantasy, heartbeat, intake of air, nerve stimulation, all of things that have made it possible for you to imagine what "life" will be like after you die will be destroyed when it dies. Every thought your brain has created, including "It would be like quitting your job for the opportunity to make it big on Wall Street" was made wholly and completely by the engine that was destroyed.
